questions.q: Why does the lesson move logic such as build_pipeline out of the notebook and into the churn/ package?
options: So the notebook, training script, tests and services all run the same importable code
Because notebooks cannot import scikit-learn
Because packages train models faster than notebooks
So the notebook can be deleted
questions.explain: An importable package is a single source of truth that every consumer of the logic can share.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of reading settings such as the test split and C from params.yaml?
options: It makes scikit-learn run in parallel
Settings can be changed, tracked and compared without editing the code
It encrypts the settings
YAML files are required by joblib
questions.explain: A config file separates settings from logic, so changes are one-line, reviewable edits that tools can also track.

questions.q: According to the lesson's rule of thumb, which items belong in Git?
options: Raw datasets and trained model files
Only notebooks
Code, configuration, requirements, tests and cleaned notebooks
Nothing; ML projects cannot use Git
questions.explain: Small text files diff well in Git. Large binary data and models get their own versioning, covered in Chapter 2.

questions.q: What is the role of the notebooks/ folder in the layout?
options: It holds the trained model
It holds the only copy of the training code
It stores the dependency list
Exploration and reports that import from the package
questions.explain: Notebooks are clients of the package: good for exploring data and drawing charts, not the source of truth.

questions.q: After the refactor, python -m churn.train reported accuracy 0.768. Why is that number worth checking?
options: It proves the model is production-ready
It matches the original notebook result, confirming the refactor changed structure but not behavior
It shows the data has no missing values
It is the maximum accuracy possible on this data
questions.explain: Comparing against the known notebook result is a simple regression check for a refactor.
